claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled "SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi" exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/.
AWS CDK ties infrastructure to AWS only, and multi-cloud with CDK is nearly impossible.
AWS CDK supports defining infrastructure only in TypeScript or Python, whereas Pulumi supports any programming language.
Pulumi deployments are faster than AWS CDK deployments because CDK relies on CloudFormation.
AWS CDK uses a CloudFormation state file, and its secrets management is limited to AWS Secrets Manager only.
SST's Ion is the code name for a new deployment engine that deploys constructs using Pulumi instead of CDK and CloudFormation, and once stable it will be released as SST v3.
SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for its providers and deployment engine and bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.
Pulumi lets you define infrastructure in TypeScript, Python, Go, or C# and deploy across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and on-premises.
A Founding Engineer at SST said Pulumi's deployment process feels like a natural extension of writing code and can handle advanced things traditional IaC tools can't.
Pulumi Crosswalk for AWS simplifies day one tasks, documented in the AWS guide at /docs/iac/guides/clouds/aws/.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` requires no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account or Pulumi Cloud; the engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST keeps its state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, deploying to AWS and more than 150 other providers.
SST's provisioning layer was built on AWS CDK and CloudFormation through 2023; the Ion rewrite began in late 2023.
Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: 'Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN).'
SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says that on `sst deploy`, resources call an embedded Pulumi engine that calls a bridged Terraform provider, which makes AWS SDK calls.
SST docs 'What is SST' say: 'SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for the providers and the deployment engine. And Terraform's providers are bridged through Pulumi.'
Gautier Blandin's article says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka's dev.to article says: 'You may notice right away the imports from Pulumi. It means the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi now.'
SST's platform package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi, @pulumi/aws, @pulumi/cloudflare, @pulumi/command, @pulumi/docker-build, @pulumi/random, @pulumi/tls and @pulumiverse/vercel.
The SST repository is now anomalyco/sst (formerly sst/sst).
Pulumi's Terraform bridge is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, network call to Pulumi Cloud, or Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API lets teams embed Pulumi programs in their own tools.
AWS exposes hundreds of resource types.
Nitric's docs state 'all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments', with official providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's Pulumi provider takes a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`.
SST does not invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly in Pulumi within an SST app.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The sst npm package gets roughly 796,000 downloads per week (796,291 for Sept 5-11, 2026).
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent.
opencode has a larger GitHub following than SST.
Terraform-bridged providers are provided by Pulumi's Terraform bridge at github.com/pulumi/pulumi-terraform-bridge.
Linked pages exist: /blog/aws-cdk-vs-pulumi-why-sst-switched/, /docs/iac/guides/basics/how-pulumi-works/, /blog/any-terraform-provider/, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
SST is a strong fit for opinionated full-stack application framework; Pulumi directly suits cross-team visibility, policy enforcement.
